page: Microsoft Azure L2s_v4 is a storage-optimized virtual machine instance deployed on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The hardware profile features an Intel Xeon 8573C processor based on the x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The compute configuration provides 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from a single physical core with multithreading enabled. The CPU includes 48 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 260 MB of L3 cache, alongside support for modern vector and matrix instructions including AVX-512 and Intel AMX. System memory totals 16.0 GB, yielding 8.0 GB per vCPU. Storage is bundled directly with a 480 GB local NVMe SSD, and the configuration contains no GPU acceleration.

Performance benchmarks show strong per-core results alongside multi-threaded throughput bounds expected from a 2-vCPU topology. In Geekbench tests, the instance scored 2138.0 in single-core performance, placing it within the upper tier of tested instances, whereas the multi-core result registered at 2622.0. PassMark metrics indicate a CPU score of 3723.78 and an extended instructions score of 2718.2. Memory throughput for uncached large blocks achieved 20.23 GB/sec for reads and 14.38 GB/sec for writes. In application-level benchmarks, the server sustained 2.85 million Redis SET operations per second and 4.16 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

The qualitative cost efficiency of the L2s_v4 is defined by its pairing of high memory density and dedicated local NVMe storage with a minimal core footprint. Incorporating direct-attached high-speed NVMe avoids reliance on network-attached block storage for latency-sensitive scratch or operational data. Compute-intensive parallel scalability is limited by the single physical core. The instance is best suited for localized caching, low-concurrency relational and NoSQL databases, small transactional systems, and lightweight I/O-intensive workloads.
description: Microsoft Azure L2s_v4 is a storage-optimized virtual machine powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at 4.2 GHz on Microsoft Hyper-V. The system provides 2 dedicated vCPUs on 1 physical core, 16.0 GB of system memory, and a bundled 480 GB local NVMe SSD, operating without discrete GPU accelerators. The x86_64 CPU supports extended instruction sets including AVX-512 and AMX. Benchmark results reflect strong single-core capabilities, achieving 2138.0 on Geekbench single-core, while overall multi-core and uncached memory bandwidth remain constrained by the dual-thread configuration. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the instance provides high memory density of 8.0 GB per core paired with direct-attached NVMe storage at an entry-level capacity. The L2s_v4 is appropriate for small transactional databases, Redis caching layers, and lightweight transactional applications requiring low-latency local storage.
